## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from publisher-disclosed practices, editorial board statements, and community-aggregator evidence (apa.org, manusights.com, scirev.org) gathered 2026-05. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Medium-High — global I/O psychology authorship; cross-cultural workplace studies regularly published (490 articles on "Gender Diversity and Inequality" per OpenAlex) |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Low-Medium — accepts non-Western data within mainstream I/O framework |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High — workplace diversity, gender, race × employment papers published with quantitative designs |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Industrial/organizational psychology — job satisfaction (1,896 articles), emotional intelligence (833), HRD/performance (542), team dynamics (483), psychometric methods |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **substantive theoretical advance in I/O psychology**, not just reported effects. Multi-study programmatic packages strongly preferred (manusights.com submission guide 2026-05).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Single-study work faces higher desk-rejection unless framed as Research Notes. Initial editorial decision in 6–10 weeks; full review with revisions 6–15 months total cycle.

### Methodological Preferences

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 5 | Dominant — controlled studies, field experiments, longitudinal surveys |
| Qualitative interviews | 1 | Rare in mainstream publication track |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Outside scope |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 2 | Accepted when proposing testable I/O theory |
| Mixed methods | 3 | Accepted with quantitative dominance |
| Meta-analysis | 5 | Welcomed; PRISMA reporting expected |
| Psychometric | 5 | Core method (394 articles on psychometric methodologies) |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | 1 — APA-style third-person scholarly register |
| **Expected density** | Almost none |
| **Writing style notes** | APA-style formal academic register; I/O psychology vocabulary (job satisfaction, organizational citizenship, transformational leadership, psychological capital); statistical reporting (effect sizes, SEM, multilevel modeling) expected |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers drawn primarily from the I/O psychology and organizational behavior community — strong representation of APA Division 14 (SIOP — Society for Industrial and Organizational Psychology) faculty and senior practitioners. Expect deep literacy in job satisfaction, emotional intelligence, HRD, team dynamics, leadership theory, and modern statistical methods. Common reviewer demands: "Theoretical contribution beyond effect demonstration?", "Multi-study replication?", "Practical implications for workplace?".

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | I/O psychology, organizational behavior, psychometrics | https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/apl |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Medium — methodological depth high; variance in non-I/O literature familiarity |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Yes (strong) |
| **Discourse community signals (editorial board)** | International I/O psychology programs; SIOP affiliations | https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/apl |

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Single-study designs without strong I/O theoretical justification (community evidence: manusights / community-source review 2026-05)
- Acceptance rate ~10–15% — highly competitive (community evidence: manusights 2026-05)
- Pure qualitative submissions without quantitative scaffolding
- Failure to disclose AI use per APA publisher policy
- Manuscripts outside I/O psychology scope

### Soft Tax

High for qualitative or single-study authors — typically requires complete restructuring. For I/O-aligned multi-study quantitative authors, soft tax is moderate: APA-style formatting, theoretical-advance articulation, engagement with current SIOP literature. Long timeline (6–15 months) is normal and should be planned for.

### Best Suited For

- Multi-study quantitative I/O psychology programs
- Job satisfaction, emotional intelligence, HRD empirical work
- Team dynamics and leadership research with novel theoretical contribution
- Workplace diversity and gender × employment studies
- Psychometric methodology contributions
- Meta-analyses of major I/O literatures

### Not Recommended For

- Pure autoethnography or first-person workplace narratives
- Single-case qualitative analyses
- Critical management / discursive workplace studies (consider organizational-studies journals)
- Authors needing rapid turnaround
- Theoretical papers without empirical test

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Personnel Psychology](./personnel-psychology.md) | Closest I/O peer; Wiley-published; comparable empirical-multistudy paradigm |
| 2 | [Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin](./personality-and-social-psychology-bulletin.md) | If the work has personality / social-psychology angle beyond workplace |
| 3 | [Journal of Personality and Social Psychology](./journal-of-personality-and-social-psychology.md) | If the work is more personality-focused than I/O; same APA family |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from a top general-psychology venue as "too applied / too I/O-focused," J Applied Psych is often a better fit because: it specializes in I/O psychology with deep reviewer-pool expertise; multi-study workplace programs are the journal's native format; and SIOP affiliation provides built-in audience.
